title: Options as key-like rights
claim: Options function similarly to a key that grants time-limited access to purchase an underlying asset at a fixed price without obligation to exercise
mechanism: Time-bound right with defined strike price
assumptions: Market conditions stable during holding period

title: Options are derivatives
claim: Options derive their value from an underlying security (stock, commodity, index, etc.) and belong to the derivatives asset class
assumptions: Underlying security is observable and tradeable

title: Options have defined risk for buyers
claim: Options buyers have defined, capped losses equal to the premium paid, unlike stocks where losses can theoretically reach 100%
mechanism: Maximum loss cap at premium payment
failure_modes: Gap risk, early assignment, broker technical failures

title: 1% risk rule for position sizing
claim: No single trade should risk more than 1% of total trading account capital; this preserves capital through streaks of losses
mechanism: Position size determined by: (Account_Risk_Dollar / Trade_Risk_Dollar) * N shares

title: 1% risk rule enables 100 consecutive losses
claim: If trader risks exactly 1% per trade, account must survive 100 consecutive losses to reach zero; this buffer protects against drawdown sequences

title: Profitable trading at 1% risk with 2% target
claim: If trading risks 1% per trade but targets 1.5-2% profit, even 50% win rate yields net gains over time

title: Fear of loss undermines strategy execution
claim: Emotional fear of losses causes traders to hesitate on strategy signals, miss entries, second-guess decisions, leading to abandoned strategies and loss of capital
mechanism: Fear triggers analysis paralysis; trader delays/avoids execution; signal opportunities expire
failure_modes: Fear justified by actual market risk

title: Greed causes overleveraging and overtrading
claim: Greed (excessive desire for profits) leads to irrational trading: overtrading, overleveraging, holding losers too long, chasing multiple markets, risking beyond capital tolerance

source.section: Greed - The Danger of Being Greedy

mechanism: Unrealistic expectations + clouded judgment → irrational position sizing and market picking
failure_modes: Margin calls force liquidation at worst prices

title: Covered calls generate passive income
claim: Selling covered call options against owned stock generates premium income while capping upside gains

source.chapter: Chapter 10: All About Buying Covered Calls

mechanism: Own 100 shares; sell 1 call contract (controls same 100 shares); collect premium immediately; capped profit at strike
failure_modes: Assignment forces stock sale at low strike

title: The Greeks measure option price sensitivity
claim: Delta, gamma, theta, vega quantify how option prices respond to underlying moves (delta), acceleration (gamma), time decay (theta), volatility (vega)
mechanism: Each Greek = partial derivative of option price with respect to market variable
assumptions: Option pricing model valid (Black-Scholes or similar)

title: Money management: position size by account percentage
claim: Trader should allocate a fixed % of account per position; with $100k account, 1-2% per trade = $1k-$2k max loss per position
mechanism: Max_Loss_Per_Trade = Account_Size * Risk_Percent; then Size = Max_Loss / Trade_Risk_Dollar

title: Leverage amplifies losses on margin calls
claim: Leverage (e.g., 2:1) amplifies both gains and losses; margin calls force liquidation of positions at worst prices, creating spiral losses
support: Narrative description of leverage risk cascade
mechanism: Leverage * Drawdown = Amplified Account Loss; Margin Call Threshold breached → Forced Liquidation at Market Price
failure_modes: Account liquidated faster than trader can react

title: Selling puts: income strategy with assignment risk
claim: Cash-secured puts: Trader deposits cash to collateral; sells put premium; if assigned, buys stock at strike; generates income but obligates purchase
mechanism: Sell 1 put; deposit strike_price * 100 in escrow; collect premium; if assigned, own 100 shares at strike price
failure_modes: Assigned at terrible price during crash
Underlying rallies (premium kept but capital wasted)

title: Spreads define risk and cap profit
claim: Spread strategies (e.g., bull call: buy lower call, sell higher call) cap both max loss and max profit; risk is known upfront

title: Book offers beginner framework but lacks rigor
claim: The book provides conceptual foundations for options trading (Greeks, strategies, risk rules) but omits backtesting methodology, empirical validation, or regime-specific guidance
support: No chapters on historical testing, statistical validation, market regimes, or live performance comparison
mechanism: Beginner books prioritize accessibility over rigor; lacks quantitative validation layer
assumptions: Reader seeks foundational understanding, not production implementation
failure_modes: Reader assumes strategies are pre-tested and robust without independent verification

title: Broker and regulatory references are time-bound
claim: References to broker platforms, fees, account minimums, regulatory frameworks (SEC rules circa 2020) require verification against current sources
support: Book explicitly references specific brokers and regulations without timestamps; 2020 publication now 4+ years old
mechanism: Regulatory changes, broker mergers, fee structures evolve; outdated references lead to incorrect setup
assumptions: Broker APIs and fee structures unchanged

title: Covered call strategy mechanics: entry, assignment, profit structure
claim: Detailed covered call execution: own underlying, sell ATM/OTM call, collect premium upfront, cap profit at strike, assignment forces sale if ITM
mechanism: Own stock at lower price; sell call at strike; if underlying > strike at expiry, assign forced sale at strike price; profit = (strike - buy_price) + premium
failure_modes: Underlying crashes below purchase price (unhedged downside)
